topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: It seems the place where time always tasted a little sweeter, where the lighting was just right and the dishes were more than just food—they were memories—will soon be nothing more than a chapter closed. They say all good things must come to an end, but it’s hard not to linger in the echo of what was. I find myself wondering if the last visit should be celebrated or quietly mourned. It’s a peculiar sort of goodbye, to a place that’s woven itself into the fabric of my routine, where the service was always warm, and the specials always hit the spot. Now, it’s down to the wire, and the silence of the impending loss hangs heavy, even as I try to savor what remains.
